question: Should the repository accept this integrated 84-file credential-ownership and cache-migration change as one release-boundary fix after refreshed macOS validation, or require it to be narrowed into separately reviewable compatibility layers?
rationale: The evidence supports the core security boundary and final-head live behavior, but accepting the integrated upgrade contract is a maintainer ownership decision rather than a mechanical correctness determination.

options.title: Approve after refreshed validation
options.body: Rebase or refresh against current main after the dashboard-test fix is available, then require the focused Claude suites and affected macOS shard to pass on the merge head.

options.title: Split compatibility layers
options.body: Keep the no-foreign-Keychain-read boundary, but move verifier or migration-heavy support work into follow-up PRs if maintainers prefer a smaller release-risk surface.

recommendation.title: Approve after refreshed validation
recommendation.body: Rebase or refresh against current main after the dashboard-test fix is available, then require the focused Claude suites and affected macOS shard to pass on the merge head.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository-level approval is needed because the PR changes authentication ownership, persisted-cache compatibility, and the release validation contract.
